# How to use the graph API[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#how-to-use-the-graph-api "Permanent link")
This guide demonstrates the basics of LangGraph's Graph API. It walks through [state](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#define-and-update-state), as well as composing common graph structures such as [sequences](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#create-a-sequence-of-steps), [branches](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#create-branches), and [loops](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#create-and-control-loops). It also covers LangGraph's control features, including the [Send API](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#map-reduce-and-the-send-api) for map-reduce workflows and the [Command API](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#combine-control-flow-and-state-updates-with-command) for combining state updates with "hops" across nodes.
## Setup[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#setup "Permanent link")
Install `langgraph`:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-0-1)pipinstall-Ulanggraph

```

Set up LangSmith for better debugging
Sign up for [LangSmith](https://smith.langchain.com/?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.105.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296) to quickly spot issues and improve the performance of your LangGraph projects. LangSmith lets you use trace data to debug, test, and monitor your LLM apps built with LangGraph — read more about how to get started in the [docs](https://docs.smith.langchain.com/?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.105.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296).
## Define and update state[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#define-and-update-state "Permanent link")
Here we show how to define and update [state](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#state) in LangGraph. We will demonstrate:
  1. How to use state to define a graph's [schema](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#schema)
  2. How to use [reducers](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#reducers) to control how state updates are processed.


### Define state[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#define-state "Permanent link")
[State](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#state) in LangGraph can be a `TypedDict`, `Pydantic` model, or dataclass. Below we will use `TypedDict`. See [this section](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#use-pydantic-models-for-graph-state) for detail on using Pydantic.
By default, graphs will have the same input and output schema, and the state determines that schema. See [this section](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#define-input-and-output-schemas) for how to define distinct input and output schemas.
Let's consider a simple example using [messages](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#messagesstate). This represents a versatile formulation of state for many LLM applications. See our [concepts page](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#working-with-messages-in-graph-state) for more detail.
_API Reference:[AnyMessage](https://python.langchain.com/api_reference/core/messages/langchain_core.messages.AnyMessage.html?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.105.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-1-1)fromlangchain_core.messagesimport AnyMessage
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-1-2)fromtyping_extensionsimport TypedDict
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-1-3)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-1-4)classState(TypedDict):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-1-5)  messages: list[AnyMessage]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-1-6)  extra_field: int

```

This state tracks a list of [message](https://python.langchain.com/docs/concepts/messages/?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.105.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296) objects, as well as an extra integer field.
### Update state[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#update-state "Permanent link")
Let's build an example graph with a single node. Our [node](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#nodes) is just a Python function that reads our graph's state and makes updates to it. The first argument to this function will always be the state:
_API Reference:[AIMessage](https://python.langchain.com/api_reference/core/messages/langchain_core.messages.ai.AIMessage.html?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.105.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-2-1)fromlangchain_core.messagesimport AIMessage
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-2-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-2-3)defnode(state: State):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-2-4)  messages = state["messages"]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-2-5)  new_message = AIMessage("Hello!")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-2-6)  return {"messages": messages + [new_message], "extra_field": 10}

```

This node simply appends a message to our message list, and populates an extra field.
Important
Nodes should return updates to the state directly, instead of mutating the state.
Let's next define a simple graph containing this node. We use [StateGraph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#stategraph) to define a graph that operates on this state. We then use [add_node](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#nodes) populate our graph.
_API Reference:[StateGraph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/graphs/#langgraph.graph.state.StateGraph)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-3-1)fromlanggraph.graphimport StateGraph
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-3-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-3-3)builder = StateGraph(State)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-3-4)builder.add_node(node)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-3-5)builder.set_entry_point("node")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-3-6)graph = builder.compile()

```

LangGraph provides built-in utilities for visualizing your graph. Let's inspect our graph. See [this section](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#visualize-your-graph) for detail on visualization.
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-4-1)fromIPython.displayimport Image, display
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-4-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-4-3)display(Image(graph.get_graph().draw_mermaid_png()))

```

![Simple graph with single node](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/assets/graph_api_image_1.png)
In this case, our graph just executes a single node. Let's proceed with a simple invocation:
_API Reference:[HumanMessage](https://python.langchain.com/api_reference/core/messages/langchain_core.messages.human.HumanMessage.html?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.105.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-5-1)fromlangchain_core.messagesimport HumanMessage
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-5-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-5-3)result = graph.invoke({"messages": [HumanMessage("Hi")]})
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-5-4)result

```

```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-6-1){'messages': [HumanMessage(content='Hi'), AIMessage(content='Hello!')], 'extra_field': 10}

```

Note that:
  * We kicked off invocation by updating a single key of the state.
  * We receive the entire state in the invocation result.


For convenience, we frequently inspect the content of [message objects](https://python.langchain.com/docs/concepts/messages/?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.105.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296) via pretty-print:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-7-1)for message in result["messages"]:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-7-2)  message.pretty_print()

```

```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-8-1)================================ Human Message ================================
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-8-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-8-3)Hi
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-8-4)================================== Ai Message ==================================
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-8-5)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-8-6)Hello!

```

### Process state updates with reducers[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#process-state-updates-with-reducers "Permanent link")
Each key in the state can have its own independent [reducer](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#reducers) function, which controls how updates from nodes are applied. If no reducer function is explicitly specified then it is assumed that all updates to the key should override it.
For `TypedDict` state schemas, we can define reducers by annotating the corresponding field of the state with a reducer function.
In the earlier example, our node updated the `"messages"` key in the state by appending a message to it. Below, we add a reducer to this key, such that updates are automatically appended:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-9-1)fromtyping_extensionsimport Annotated
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-9-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-9-3)defadd(left, right):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-9-4)"""Can also import `add` from the `operator` built-in."""
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-9-5)  return left + right
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-9-6)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-9-7)classState(TypedDict):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-9-8)  messages: Annotated[list[AnyMessage], add]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-9-9)  extra_field: int

```

Now our node can be simplified:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-10-1)defnode(state: State):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-10-2)  new_message = AIMessage("Hello!")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-10-3)  return {"messages": [new_message], "extra_field": 10}

```

_API Reference:[START](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/constants/#langgraph.constants.START)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-11-1)fromlanggraph.graphimport START
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-11-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-11-3)graph = StateGraph(State).add_node(node).add_edge(START, "node").compile()
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-11-4)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-11-5)result = graph.invoke({"messages": [HumanMessage("Hi")]})
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-11-6)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-11-7)for message in result["messages"]:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-11-8)  message.pretty_print()

```

```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-12-1)================================ Human Message ================================
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-12-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-12-3)Hi
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-12-4)================================== Ai Message ==================================
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-12-5)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-12-6)Hello!

```

#### MessagesState[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#messagesstate "Permanent link")
In practice, there are additional considerations for updating lists of messages:
  * We may wish to update an existing message in the state.
  * We may want to accept short-hands for [message formats](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#using-messages-in-your-graph), such as [OpenAI format](https://python.langchain.com/docs/concepts/messages/?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.105.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296#openai-format).


LangGraph includes a built-in reducer `add_messages` that handles these considerations:
_API Reference:[add_messages](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/graphs/#langgraph.graph.message.add_messages)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-13-1)fromlanggraph.graph.messageimport add_messages
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-13-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-13-3)classState(TypedDict):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-13-4)  messages: Annotated[list[AnyMessage], add_messages]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-13-5)  extra_field: int
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-13-6)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-13-7)defnode(state: State):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-13-8)  new_message = AIMessage("Hello!")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-13-9)  return {"messages": [new_message], "extra_field": 10}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-13-10)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-13-11)graph = StateGraph(State).add_node(node).set_entry_point("node").compile()

```

```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-14-1)input_message = {"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-14-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-14-3)result = graph.invoke({"messages": [input_message]})
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-14-4)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-14-5)for message in result["messages"]:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-14-6)  message.pretty_print()

```

```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-15-1)================================ Human Message ================================
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-15-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-15-3)Hi
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-15-4)================================== Ai Message ==================================
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-15-5)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-15-6)Hello!

```

This is a versatile representation of state for applications involving [chat models](https://python.langchain.com/docs/concepts/chat_models/?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.105.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296). LangGraph includes a pre-built `MessagesState` for convenience, so that we can have:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-16-1)fromlanggraph.graphimport MessagesState
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-16-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-16-3)classState(MessagesState):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-16-4)  extra_field: int

```

### Define input and output schemas[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#define-input-and-output-schemas "Permanent link")
By default, `StateGraph` operates with a single schema, and all nodes are expected to communicate using that schema. However, it's also possible to define distinct input and output schemas for a graph.
When distinct schemas are specified, an internal schema will still be used for communication between nodes. The input schema ensures that the provided input matches the expected structure, while the output schema filters the internal data to return only the relevant information according to the defined output schema.
Below, we'll see how to define distinct input and output schema.
_API Reference:[StateGraph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/graphs/#langgraph.graph.state.StateGraph) | [START](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/constants/#langgraph.constants.START) | [END](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/constants/#langgraph.constants.END)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-17-1)fromlanggraph.graphimport StateGraph, START, END
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-17-2)fromtyping_extensionsimport TypedDict

### Pass private state between nodes[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#pass-private-state-between-nodes "Permanent link")
In some cases, you may want nodes to exchange information that is crucial for intermediate logic but doesn't need to be part of the main schema of the graph. This private data is not relevant to the overall input/output of the graph and should only be shared between certain nodes.
Below, we'll create an example sequential graph consisting of three nodes (node_1, node_2 and node_3), where private data is passed between the first two steps (node_1 and node_2), while the third step (node_3) only has access to the public overall state.
_API Reference:[StateGraph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/graphs/#langgraph.graph.state.StateGraph) | [START](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/constants/#langgraph.constants.START) | [END](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/constants/#langgraph.constants.END)_
```

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-2)fromtyping_extensionsimport TypedDict
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-3)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-4)# The overall state of the graph (this is the public state shared across nodes)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-5)classOverallState(TypedDict):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-6)  a: str
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-7)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-8)# Output from node_1 contains private data that is not part of the overall state

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-10)  private_data: str

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-14)  output = {"private_data": "set by node_1"}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-15)  print(f"Entered node `node_1`:\n\tInput: {state}.\n\tReturned: {output}")

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-17)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-18)# Node 2 input only requests the private data available after node_1

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-20)  private_data: str
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-21)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-22)defnode_2(state: Node2Input) -> OverallState:

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-24)  print(f"Entered node `node_2`:\n\tInput: {state}.\n\tReturned: {output}")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-25)  return output
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-26)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-27)# Node 3 only has access to the overall state (no access to private data from node_1)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-28)defnode_3(state: OverallState) -> OverallState:

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-31)  return output

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-33)# Connect nodes in a sequence
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-34)# node_2 accepts private data from node_1, whereas

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-36)builder = StateGraph(OverallState).add_sequence([node_1, node_2, node_3])

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-38)graph = builder.compile()
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-39)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-40)# Invoke the graph with the initial state
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-19-41)response = graph.invoke(

### Use Pydantic models for graph state[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#use-pydantic-models-for-graph-state "Permanent link")
A [StateGraph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/graphs.md#langgraph.graph.StateGraph) accepts a `state_schema` argument on initialization that specifies the "shape" of the state that the nodes in the graph can access and update.
In our examples, we typically use a python-native `TypedDict` or [`dataclass`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/dataclasses.html) for `state_schema`, but `state_schema` can be any [type](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#type-objects).
Here, we'll see how a [Pydantic BaseModel](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/api/base_model/) can be used for `state_schema` to add run-time validation on **inputs**.
Known Limitations
  * Currently, the output of the graph will **NOT** be an instance of a pydantic model.
  * Run-time validation only occurs on inputs into nodes, not on the outputs.
  * The validation error trace from pydantic does not show which node the error arises in.
  * Pydantic's recursive validation can be slow. For performance-sensitive applications, you may want to consider using a `dataclass` instead.


_API Reference:[StateGraph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/graphs/#langgraph.graph.state.StateGraph) | [START](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/constants/#langgraph.constants.START) | [END](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/constants/#langgraph.constants.END)_
```

See below for additional features of Pydantic model state:
Serialization Behavior
When using Pydantic models as state schemas, it's important to understand how serialization works, especially when: - Passing Pydantic objects as inputs - Receiving outputs from the graph - Working with nested Pydantic models
Let's see these behaviors in action.
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-1)fromlanggraph.graphimport StateGraph, START, END
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-2)frompydanticimport BaseModel
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-3)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-4)classNestedModel(BaseModel):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-5)  value: str
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-6)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-7)classComplexState(BaseModel):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-8)  text: str
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-9)  count: int
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-10)  nested: NestedModel
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-11)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-12)defprocess_node(state: ComplexState):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-13)  # Node receives a validated Pydantic object
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-14)  print(f"Input state type: {type(state)}")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-15)  print(f"Nested type: {type(state.nested)}")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-16)  # Return a dictionary update
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-17)  return {"text": state.text + " processed", "count": state.count + 1}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-18)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-19)# Build the graph
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-20)builder = StateGraph(ComplexState)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-21)builder.add_node("process", process_node)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-22)builder.add_edge(START, "process")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-23)builder.add_edge("process", END)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-24)graph = builder.compile()
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-25)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-26)# Create a Pydantic instance for input

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-28)print(f"Input object type: {type(input_state)}")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-24-29)

Runtime Type Coercion
Pydantic performs runtime type coercion for certain data types. This can be helpful but also lead to unexpected behavior if you're not aware of it.
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-25-1)fromlanggraph.graphimport StateGraph, START, END

Working with Message Models
When working with LangChain message types in your state schema, there are important considerations for serialization. You should use `AnyMessage` (rather than `BaseMessage`) for proper serialization/deserialization when using message objects over the wire.
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-1)fromlanggraph.graphimport StateGraph, START, END
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-2)frompydanticimport BaseModel
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-3)fromlangchain_core.messagesimport HumanMessage, AIMessage, AnyMessage
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-4)fromtypingimport List
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-5)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-6)classChatState(BaseModel):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-7)  messages: List[AnyMessage]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-8)  context: str
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-9)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-10)defadd_message(state: ChatState):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-11)  return {"messages": state.messages + [AIMessage(content="Hello there!")]}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-12)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-13)builder = StateGraph(ChatState)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-14)builder.add_node("add_message", add_message)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-15)builder.add_edge(START, "add_message")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-16)builder.add_edge("add_message", END)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-17)graph = builder.compile()
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-18)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-19)# Create input with a message
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-20)initial_state = ChatState(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-21)  messages=[HumanMessage(content="Hi")], context="Customer support chat"
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-22))
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-23)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-24)result = graph.invoke(initial_state)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-25)print(f"Output: {result}")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-26)

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-26-29)for i, msg in enumerate(output_model.messages):

## Add runtime configuration[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#add-runtime-configuration "Permanent link")
Sometimes you want to be able to configure your graph when calling it. For example, you might want to be able to specify what LLM or system prompt to use at runtime, _without polluting the graph state with these parameters_.
To add runtime configuration:
  1. Specify a schema for your configuration
  2. Add the configuration to the function signature for nodes or conditional edges
  3. Pass the configuration into the graph.


See below for a simple example:
_API Reference:[RunnableConfig](https://python.langchain.com/api_reference/core/runnables/langchain_core.runnables.config.RunnableConfig.html?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.105.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296) | [END](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/constants/#langgraph.constants.END) | [StateGraph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/graphs/#langgraph.graph.state.StateGraph) | [START](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/constants/#langgraph.constants.START)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-1)fromlangchain_core.runnablesimport RunnableConfig
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-2)fromlanggraph.graphimport END, StateGraph, START
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-3)fromtyping_extensionsimport TypedDict
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-4)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-5)# 1. Specify config schema
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-6)classConfigSchema(TypedDict):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-7)  my_runtime_value: str
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-8)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-9)# 2. Define a graph that accesses the config in a node
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-10)classState(TypedDict):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-11)  my_state_value: str
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-12)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-13)defnode(state: State, config: RunnableConfig):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-14)  if config["configurable"]["my_runtime_value"] == "a":
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-15)    return {"my_state_value": 1}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-16)  elif config["configurable"]["my_runtime_value"] == "b":
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-17)    return {"my_state_value": 2}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-18)  else:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-19)    raise ValueError("Unknown values.")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-20)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-21)builder = StateGraph(State, config_schema=ConfigSchema)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-22)builder.add_node(node)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-23)builder.add_edge(START, "node")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-24)builder.add_edge("node", END)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-25)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-26)graph = builder.compile()
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-27)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-28)# 3. Pass in configuration at runtime:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-29)print(graph.invoke({}, {"configurable": {"my_runtime_value": "a"}}))
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-27-30)print(graph.invoke({}, {"configurable": {"my_runtime_value": "b"}}))

```

Extended example: specifying LLM at runtime
Below we demonstrate a practical example in which we configure what LLM to use at runtime. We will use both OpenAI and Anthropic models.
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-1)fromlangchain.chat_modelsimport init_chat_model
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-2)fromlangchain_core.runnablesimport RunnableConfig
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-3)fromlanggraph.graphimport MessagesState
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-4)fromlanggraph.graphimport END, StateGraph, START
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-5)fromtyping_extensionsimport TypedDict
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-6)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-7)classConfigSchema(TypedDict):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-8)  model: str
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-9)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-10)MODELS = {
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-11)  "anthropic": init_chat_model("anthropic:claude-3-5-haiku-latest"),
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-12)  "openai": init_chat_model("openai:gpt-4.1-mini"),
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-13)}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-14)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-15)defcall_model(state: MessagesState, config: RunnableConfig):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-16)  model = config["configurable"].get("model", "anthropic")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-17)  model = MODELS[model]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-18)  response = model.invoke(state["messages"])
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-19)  return {"messages": [response]}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-20)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-21)builder = StateGraph(MessagesState, config_schema=ConfigSchema)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-22)builder.add_node("model", call_model)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-23)builder.add_edge(START, "model")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-29-24)builder.add_edge("model", END)

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-31-36)response = graph.invoke({"messages": [input_message]}, config)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-31-37)for message in response["messages"]:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-31-38)  message.pretty_print()

```

```

## Add retry policies[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#add-retry-policies "Permanent link")
There are many use cases where you may wish for your node to have a custom retry policy, for example if you are calling an API, querying a database, or calling an LLM, etc. LangGraph lets you add retry policies to nodes.
To configure a retry policy, pass the `retry_policy` parameter to the [add_node](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/graphs/#langgraph.graph.state.StateGraph.add_node). The `retry_policy` parameter takes in a `RetryPolicy` named tuple object. Below we instantiate a `RetryPolicy` object with the default parameters and associate it with a node:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-33-1)fromlanggraph.pregelimport RetryPolicy
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-33-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-33-3)builder.add_node(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-33-4)  "node_name",
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-33-5)  node_function,
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-33-6)  retry_policy=RetryPolicy(),
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-33-7))

```

By default, the `retry_on` parameter uses the `default_retry_on` function, which retries on any exception except for the following:
  * `ValueError`
  * `TypeError`
  * `ArithmeticError`
  * `ImportError`
  * `LookupError`
  * `NameError`
  * `SyntaxError`
  * `RuntimeError`
  * `ReferenceError`
  * `StopIteration`
  * `StopAsyncIteration`
  * `OSError`


In addition, for exceptions from popular http request libraries such as `requests` and `httpx` it only retries on 5xx status codes.
Extended example: customizing retry policies
Consider an example in which we are reading from a SQL database. Below we pass two different retry policies to nodes:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-1)importsqlite3
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-2)fromtyping_extensionsimport TypedDict
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-3)fromlangchain.chat_modelsimport init_chat_model
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-4)fromlanggraph.graphimport END, MessagesState, StateGraph, START
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-5)fromlanggraph.pregelimport RetryPolicy
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-6)fromlangchain_community.utilitiesimport SQLDatabase
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-7)fromlangchain_core.messagesimport AIMessage
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-8)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-9)db = SQLDatabase.from_uri("sqlite:///:memory:")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-10)model = init_chat_model("anthropic:claude-3-5-haiku-latest")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-11)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-12)defquery_database(state: MessagesState):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-13)  query_result = db.run("SELECT * FROM Artist LIMIT 10;")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-14)  return {"messages": [AIMessage(content=query_result)]}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-15)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-16)defcall_model(state: MessagesState):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-17)  response = model.invoke(state["messages"])
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-18)  return {"messages": [response]}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-19)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-20)# Define a new graph
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-21)builder = StateGraph(MessagesState)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-22)builder.add_node(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-23)  "query_database",
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-24)  query_database,
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-25)  retry_policy=RetryPolicy(retry_on=sqlite3.OperationalError),
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-26))
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-27)builder.add_node("model", call_model, retry_policy=RetryPolicy(max_attempts=5))
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-28)builder.add_edge(START, "model")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-29)builder.add_edge("model", "query_database")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-30)builder.add_edge("query_database", END)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-34-31)graph = builder.compile()

```

## Add node caching[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#add-node-caching "Permanent link")
Node caching is useful in cases where you want to avoid repeating operations, like when doing something expensive (either in terms of time or cost). LangGraph lets you add individualized caching policies to nodes in a graph.
To configure a cache policy, pass the `cache_policy` parameter to the [add_node](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/graphs.md#langgraph.graph.state.StateGraph.add_node) function. In the following example, a [`CachePolicy`](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/types/?h=cachepolicy#langgraph.types.CachePolicy) object is instantiated with a time to live of 120 seconds and the default `key_func` generator. Then it is associated with a node:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-35-1)fromlanggraph.typesimport CachePolicy
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-35-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-35-3)builder.add_node(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-35-4)  "node_name",
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-35-5)  node_function,
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-35-6)  cache_policy=CachePolicy(ttl=120),
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-35-7))

```

Then, to enable node-level caching for a graph, set the `cache` argument when compiling the graph. The example below uses `InMemoryCache` to set up a graph with in-memory cache, but `SqliteCache` is also available.
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-36-1)fromlanggraph.cache.memoryimport InMemoryCache
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-36-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-36-3)graph = builder.compile(cache=InMemoryCache())

```

## Create a sequence of steps[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#create-a-sequence-of-steps "Permanent link")
Prerequisites
This guide assumes familiarity with the above section on [state](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#define-and-update-state).
Here we demonstrate how to construct a simple sequence of steps. We will show:
  1. How to build a sequential graph
  2. Built-in short-hand for constructing similar graphs.


To add a sequence of nodes, we use the `.add_node` and `.add_edge` methods of our [graph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#stategraph):
_API Reference:[START](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/constants/#langgraph.constants.START) | [StateGraph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/graphs/#langgraph.graph.state.StateGraph)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-37-1)fromlanggraph.graphimport START, StateGraph
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-37-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-37-3)builder = StateGraph(State)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-37-4)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-37-5)# Add nodes
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-37-6)builder.add_node(step_1)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-37-7)builder.add_node(step_2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-37-8)builder.add_node(step_3)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-37-9)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-37-10)# Add edges
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-37-11)builder.add_edge(START, "step_1")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-37-12)builder.add_edge("step_1", "step_2")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-37-13)builder.add_edge("step_2", "step_3")

```

We can also use the built-in shorthand `.add_sequence`:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-38-1)builder = StateGraph(State).add_sequence([step_1, step_2, step_3])
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-38-2)builder.add_edge(START, "step_1")

```

Why split application steps into a sequence with LangGraph?
LangGraph makes it easy to add an underlying persistence layer to your application. This allows state to be checkpointed in between the execution of nodes, so your LangGraph nodes govern:
  * How state updates are [checkpointed](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/persistence/)
  * How interruptions are resumed in [human-in-the-loop](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/human_in_the_loop/) workflows
  * How we can "rewind" and branch-off executions using LangGraph's [time travel](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/time-travel/) features


They also determine how execution steps are [streamed](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/streaming/), and how your application is visualized and debugged using [LangGraph Studio](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/langgraph_studio/).
Let's demonstrate an end-to-end example. We will create a sequence of three steps:
  1. Populate a value in a key of the state
  2. Update the same value
  3. Populate a different value


Let's first define our [state](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#state). This governs the [schema of the graph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#schema), and can also specify how to apply updates. See [this section](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#process-state-updates-with-reducers) for more detail.
In our case, we will just keep track of two values:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-39-1)fromtyping_extensionsimport TypedDict
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-39-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-39-3)classState(TypedDict):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-39-4)  value_1: str
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-39-5)  value_2: int

```

Our [nodes](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#nodes) are just Python functions that read our graph's state and make updates to it. The first argument to this function will always be the state:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-40-1)defstep_1(state: State):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-40-2)  return {"value_1": "a"}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-40-3)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-40-4)defstep_2(state: State):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-40-5)  current_value_1 = state["value_1"]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-40-6)  return {"value_1": f"{current_value_1} b"}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-40-7)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-40-8)defstep_3(state: State):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-40-9)  return {"value_2": 10}

```

Note
Note that when issuing updates to the state, each node can just specify the value of the key it wishes to update.
By default, this will **overwrite** the value of the corresponding key. You can also use [reducers](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#reducers) to control how updates are processed— for example, you can append successive updates to a key instead. See [this section](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#process-state-updates-with-reducers) for more detail.
Finally, we define the graph. We use [StateGraph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#stategraph) to define a graph that operates on this state.
We will then use [add_node](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#messagesstate) and [add_edge](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#edges) to populate our graph and define its control flow.
_API Reference:[START](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/constants/#langgraph.constants.START) | [StateGraph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/graphs/#langgraph.graph.state.StateGraph)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-41-1)fromlanggraph.graphimport START, StateGraph
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-41-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-41-3)builder = StateGraph(State)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-41-4)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-41-5)# Add nodes
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-41-6)builder.add_node(step_1)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-41-7)builder.add_node(step_2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-41-8)builder.add_node(step_3)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-41-9)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-41-10)# Add edges
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-41-11)builder.add_edge(START, "step_1")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-41-12)builder.add_edge("step_1", "step_2")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-41-13)builder.add_edge("step_2", "step_3")

```

Specifying custom names
You can specify custom names for nodes using `.add_node`:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-42-1)builder.add_node("my_node", step_1)

```

Note that:
  * `.add_edge` takes the names of nodes, which for functions defaults to `node.__name__`.
  * We must specify the entry point of the graph. For this we add an edge with the [START node](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#start-node).
  * The graph halts when there are no more nodes to execute.


We next [compile](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#compiling-your-graph) our graph. This provides a few basic checks on the structure of the graph (e.g., identifying orphaned nodes). If we were adding persistence to our application via a [checkpointer](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/persistence/), it would also be passed in here.
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-43-1)graph = builder.compile()

```

LangGraph provides built-in utilities for visualizing your graph. Let's inspect our sequence. See [this guide](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#visualize-your-graph) for detail on visualization.
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-44-1)fromIPython.displayimport Image, display
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-44-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-44-3)display(Image(graph.get_graph().draw_mermaid_png()))

```

![Sequence of steps graph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/assets/graph_api_image_2.png)
Let's proceed with a simple invocation:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-45-1)graph.invoke({"value_1": "c"})

```

```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-46-1){'value_1': 'a b', 'value_2': 10}

```

Note that:
  * We kicked off invocation by providing a value for a single state key. We must always provide a value for at least one key.
  * The value we passed in was overwritten by the first node.
  * The second node updated the value.
  * The third node populated a different value.


Built-in shorthand
`langgraph>=0.2.46` includes a built-in short-hand `add_sequence` for adding node sequences. You can compile the same graph as follows:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-47-1)builder = StateGraph(State).add_sequence([step_1, step_2, step_3])
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-47-2)builder.add_edge(START, "step_1")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-47-3)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-47-4)graph = builder.compile()
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-47-5)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-47-6)graph.invoke({"value_1": "c"})  

```

## Create branches[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#create-branches "Permanent link")
Parallel execution of nodes is essential to speed up overall graph operation. LangGraph offers native support for parallel execution of nodes, which can significantly enhance the performance of graph-based workflows. This parallelization is achieved through fan-out and fan-in mechanisms, utilizing both standard edges and [conditional_edges](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/graphs.md#langgraph.graph.MessageGraph.add_conditional_edges). Below are some examples showing how to add create branching dataflows that work for you.
### Run graph nodes in parallel[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#run-graph-nodes-in-parallel "Permanent link")
In this example, we fan out from `Node A` to `B and C` and then fan in to `D`. With our state, [we specify the reducer add operation](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level.md#reducers). This will combine or accumulate values for the specific key in the State, rather than simply overwriting the existing value. For lists, this means concatenating the new list with the existing list. See the above section on [state reducers](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#process-state-updates-with-reducers) for more detail on updating state with reducers.
_API Reference:[StateGraph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/graphs/#langgraph.graph.state.StateGraph) | [START](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/constants/#langgraph.constants.START) | [END](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/constants/#langgraph.constants.END)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-48-1)importoperator

![Parallel execution graph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/assets/graph_api_image_3.png)
With the reducer, you can see that the values added in each node are accumulated.
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-50-1)graph.invoke({"aggregate": []}, {"configurable": {"thread_id": "foo"}})

```

```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-51-1)Adding "A" to []
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-51-2)Adding "B" to ['A']
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-51-3)Adding "C" to ['A']
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-51-4)Adding "D" to ['A', 'B', 'C']

```

Note
In the above example, nodes `"b"` and `"c"` are executed concurrently in the same [superstep](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#graphs). Because they are in the same step, node `"d"` executes after both `"b"` and `"c"` are finished.
Importantly, updates from a parallel superstep may not be ordered consistently. If you need a consistent, predetermined ordering of updates from a parallel superstep, you should write the outputs to a separate field in the state together with a value with which to order them.
Exception handling?
LangGraph executes nodes within [supersteps](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#graphs), meaning that while parallel branches are executed in parallel, the entire superstep is **transactional**. If any of these branches raises an exception, **none** of the updates are applied to the state (the entire superstep errors).
Importantly, when using a [checkpointer](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/persistence/), results from successful nodes within a superstep are saved, and don't repeat when resumed.
If you have error-prone (perhaps want to handle flakey API calls), LangGraph provides two ways to address this:
  1. You can write regular python code within your node to catch and handle exceptions.
  2. You can set a **[retry_policy](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/types/#langgraph.types.RetryPolicy)** to direct the graph to retry nodes that raise certain types of exceptions. Only failing branches are retried, so you needn't worry about performing redundant work.


Together, these let you perform parallel execution and fully control exception handling.
### Defer node execution[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#defer-node-execution "Permanent link")
Deferring node execution is useful when you want to delay the execution of a node until all other pending tasks are completed. This is particularly relevant when branches have different lengths, which is common in workflows like map-reduce flows.
The above example showed how to fan-out and fan-in when each path was only one step. But what if one branch had more than one step? Let's add a node `"b_2"` in the `"b"` branch:

In the above example, nodes `"b"` and `"c"` are executed concurrently in the same superstep. We set `defer=True` on node `d` so it will not execute until all pending tasks are finished. In this case, this means that `"d"` waits to execute until the entire `"b"` branch is finished.
### Conditional branching[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#conditional-branching "Permanent link")
If your fan-out should vary at runtime based on the state, you can use [add_conditional_edges](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/graphs.md#langgraph.graph.StateGraph.add_conditional_edges) to select one or more paths using the graph state. See example below, where node `a` generates a state update that determines the following node.
_API Reference:[StateGraph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/graphs/#langgraph.graph.state.StateGraph) | [START](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/constants/#langgraph.constants.START) | [END](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/constants/#langgraph.constants.END)_

## Map-Reduce and the Send API[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#map-reduce-and-the-send-api "Permanent link")
LangGraph supports map-reduce and other advanced branching patterns using the Send API. Here is an example of how to use it:

## Create and control loops[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#create-and-control-loops "Permanent link")
When creating a graph with a loop, we require a mechanism for terminating execution. This is most commonly done by adding a [conditional edge](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#conditional-edges) that routes to the [END](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#end-node) node once we reach some termination condition.
You can also set the graph recursion limit when invoking or streaming the graph. The recursion limit sets the number of [supersteps](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#graphs) that the graph is allowed to execute before it raises an error. Read more about the concept of recursion limits [here](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#recursion-limit).
Let's consider a simple graph with a loop to better understand how these mechanisms work.
Tip
To return the last value of your state instead of receiving a recursion limit error, see the [next section](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#impose-a-recursion-limit).
When creating a loop, you can include a conditional edge that specifies a termination condition:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-65-1)builder = StateGraph(State)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-65-2)builder.add_node(a)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-65-3)builder.add_node(b)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-65-4)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-65-5)defroute(state: State) -> Literal["b", END]:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-65-6)  if termination_condition(state):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-65-7)    return END
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-65-8)  else:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-65-9)    return "b"
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-65-10)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-65-11)builder.add_edge(START, "a")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-65-12)builder.add_conditional_edges("a", route)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-65-13)builder.add_edge("b", "a")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-65-14)graph = builder.compile()

```

To control the recursion limit, specify `"recursion_limit"` in the config. This will raise a `GraphRecursionError`, which you can catch and handle:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-66-1)fromlanggraph.errorsimport GraphRecursionError
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-66-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-66-3)try:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-66-4)  graph.invoke(inputs, {"recursion_limit": 3})
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-66-5)except GraphRecursionError:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-66-6)  print("Recursion Error")

```

Let's define a graph with a simple loop. Note that we use a conditional edge to implement a termination condition.

![Simple loop graph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/assets/graph_api_image_3.png)
This architecture is similar to a [ReAct agent](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/agents/overview/) in which node `"a"` is a tool-calling model, and node `"b"` represents the tools.
In our `route` conditional edge, we specify that we should end after the `"aggregate"` list in the state passes a threshold length.
Invoking the graph, we see that we alternate between nodes `"a"` and `"b"` before terminating once we reach the termination condition.
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-69-1)graph.invoke({"aggregate": []})

```

### Impose a recursion limit[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#impose-a-recursion-limit "Permanent link")
In some applications, we may not have a guarantee that we will reach a given termination condition. In these cases, we can set the graph's [recursion limit](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#recursion-limit). This will raise a `GraphRecursionError` after a given number of [supersteps](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#graphs). We can then catch and handle this exception:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-71-1)fromlanggraph.errorsimport GraphRecursionError
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-71-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-71-3)try:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-71-4)  graph.invoke({"aggregate": []}, {"recursion_limit": 4})
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-71-5)except GraphRecursionError:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-71-6)  print("Recursion Error")

```

```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-72-1)Node A sees []
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-72-2)Node B sees ['A']
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-72-3)Node C sees ['A', 'B']
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-72-4)Node D sees ['A', 'B']
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-72-5)Node A sees ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D']
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-72-6)Recursion Error

```

Extended example: return state on hitting recursion limit
Instead of raising `GraphRecursionError`, we can introduce a new key to the state that keeps track of the number of steps remaining until reaching the recursion limit. We can then use this key to determine if we should end the run.
LangGraph implements a special `RemainingSteps` annotation. Under the hood, it creates a `ManagedValue` channel -- a state channel that will exist for the duration of our graph run and no longer.
```

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-73-6)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-73-7)classState(TypedDict):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-73-8)  aggregate: Annotated[list, operator.add]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-73-9)  remaining_steps: RemainingSteps

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-73-14)

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-73-17)  return {"aggregate": ["B"]}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-73-18)

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-73-21)builder.add_node(a)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-73-22)builder.add_node(b)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-73-23)

![Complex loop graph with branches](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/assets/graph_api_image_8.png)
This graph looks complex, but can be conceptualized as loop of [supersteps](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#graphs):
  1. Node A
  2. Node B
  3. Nodes C and D
  4. Node A
  5. ...


We have a loop of four supersteps, where nodes C and D are executed concurrently.
Invoking the graph as before, we see that we complete two full "laps" before hitting the termination condition:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-77-1)result = graph.invoke({"aggregate": []})

```

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-78-5)Node A sees ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D']
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-78-6)Node B sees ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'A']
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-78-7)Node D sees ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'A', 'B']

## Async[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#async "Permanent link")
Using the [async](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio.html) programming paradigm can produce significant performance improvements when running [IO-bound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I/O_bound) code concurrently (e.g., making concurrent API requests to a chat model provider).
To convert a `sync` implementation of the graph to an `async` implementation, you will need to:
  1. Update `nodes` use `async def` instead of `def`.
  2. Update the code inside to use `await` appropriately.
  3. Invoke the graph with `.ainvoke` or `.astream` as desired.


Because many LangChain objects implement the [Runnable Protocol](https://python.langchain.com/docs/expression_language/interface/?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.105.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296) which has `async` variants of all the `sync` methods it's typically fairly quick to upgrade a `sync` graph to an `async` graph.
See example below. To demonstrate async invocations of underlying LLMs, we will include a chat model:
[OpenAI](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__tabbed_1_1)[Anthropic](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__tabbed_1_2)[Azure](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__tabbed_1_3)[Google Gemini](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__tabbed_1_4)[AWS Bedrock](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__tabbed_1_5)
```

Async streaming
See the [streaming guide](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/streaming/) for examples of streaming with async.
## Combine control flow and state updates with `Command`[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#combine-control-flow-and-state-updates-with-command "Permanent link")
It can be useful to combine control flow (edges) and state updates (nodes). For example, you might want to BOTH perform state updates AND decide which node to go to next in the SAME node. LangGraph provides a way to do so by returning a [Command](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/types/#langgraph.types.Command) object from node functions:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-92-1)defmy_node(state: State) -> Command[Literal["my_other_node"]]:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-92-2)  return Command(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-92-3)    # state update
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-92-4)    update={"foo": "bar"},
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-92-5)    # control flow
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-92-6)    goto="my_other_node"
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-92-7)  )

```

We show an end-to-end example below. Let's create a simple graph with 3 nodes: A, B and C. We will first execute node A, and then decide whether to go to Node B or Node C next based on the output of node A.
_API Reference:[StateGraph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/graphs/#langgraph.graph.state.StateGraph) | [START](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/constants/#langgraph.constants.START) | [Command](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/types/#langgraph.types.Command)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-93-1)importrandom
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-93-2)fromtyping_extensionsimport TypedDict, Literal
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-93-3)fromlanggraph.graphimport StateGraph, START
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-93-4)fromlanggraph.typesimport Command
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-93-5)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-93-6)# Define graph state
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-93-7)classState(TypedDict):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-93-8)  foo: str
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-93-9)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-93-10)# Define the nodes
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-93-11)

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-93-13)  print("Called A")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-93-14)  value = random.choice(["a", "b"])
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-93-15)  # this is a replacement for a conditional edge function
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/graph-api/#__codelineno-93-16)  if value == "a":
