## Context management[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#context-management "Permanent link")
Tools within LangGraph sometimes require context data, such as runtime-only arguments (e.g., user IDs or session details), that should not be controlled by the model. LangGraph provides three methods for managing such context:
Type | Usage Scenario | Mutable | Lifetime  
---|---|---|---  
[Configuration](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#configuration) | Static, immutable runtime data | ❌ | Single invocation  
[Short-term memory](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#short-term-memory) | Dynamic, changing data during invocation | ✅ | Single invocation  
[Long-term memory](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#long-term-memory) | Persistent, cross-session data | ✅ | Across multiple sessions  
### Configuration[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#configuration "Permanent link")
Use configuration when you have **immutable** runtime data that tools require, such as user identifiers. You pass these arguments via [`RunnableConfig`](https://python.langchain.com/docs/concepts/runnables/?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.116.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296#runnableconfig) at invocation and access them in the tool:
_API Reference:[tool](https://python.langchain.com/api_reference/core/tools/langchain_core.tools.convert.tool.html?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.116.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296) | [RunnableConfig](https://python.langchain.com/api_reference/core/runnables/langchain_core.runnables.config.RunnableConfig.html?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.116.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296)_
```

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-20-2)fromlangchain_core.runnablesimport RunnableConfig

### Short-term memory[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#short-term-memory "Permanent link")
Short-term memory maintains **dynamic** state that changes during a single execution. 
To **access** (read) the graph state inside the tools, you can use a special parameter **annotation** — [`InjectedState`](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/agents/#langgraph.prebuilt.tool_node.InjectedState "<code class="doc-symbol doc-symbol-heading doc-symbol-class"></code>      <span class="doc doc-object-name doc-class-name">InjectedState</span>"): 
_API Reference:[tool](https://python.langchain.com/api_reference/core/tools/langchain_core.tools.convert.tool.html?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.116.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296) | [InjectedState](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/prebuilt/#langgraph.prebuilt.tool_node.InjectedState) | [create_react_agent](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/prebuilt/#langgraph.prebuilt.chat_agent_executor.create_react_agent) | [AgentState](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/prebuilt/#langgraph.prebuilt.chat_agent_executor.AgentState)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-22-1)fromtypingimport Annotated, NotRequired
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-22-2)fromlangchain_core.toolsimport tool
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-22-3)fromlanggraph.prebuiltimport InjectedState, create_react_agent
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-22-4)fromlanggraph.prebuilt.chat_agent_executorimport AgentState
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-22-5)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-22-6)classCustomState(AgentState):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-22-7)  # The user_name field in short-term state
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-22-8)  user_name: NotRequired[str]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-22-9)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-22-10)@tool

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-22-12)  state: Annotated[CustomState, InjectedState]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-22-13)) -> str:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-22-14)"""Retrieve the current user-name from state."""
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-22-15)  # Return stored name or a default if not set
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-22-16)  return state.get("user_name", "Unknown user")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-22-17)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-22-18)# Example agent setup

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-22-21)  tools=[get_user_name],

Use a tool that returns a `Command` to **update** `user_name` and append a confirmation message:
_API Reference:[Command](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/types/#langgraph.types.Command) | [ToolMessage](https://python.langchain.com/api_reference/core/messages/langchain_core.messages.tool.ToolMessage.html?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.116.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296) | [tool](https://python.langchain.com/api_reference/core/tools/langchain_core.tools.convert.tool.html?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.116.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296) | [InjectedToolCallId](https://python.langchain.com/api_reference/core/tools/langchain_core.tools.base.InjectedToolCallId.html?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.116.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296)_

Important
If you want to use tools that return `Command` and update graph state, you can either use prebuilt [`create_react_agent`](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/agents/#langgraph.prebuilt.chat_agent_executor.create_react_agent "<code class="doc-symbol doc-symbol-heading doc-symbol-function"></code>      <span class="doc doc-object-name doc-function-name">create_react_agent</span>") / [`ToolNode`](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/agents/#langgraph.prebuilt.tool_node.ToolNode "<code class="doc-symbol doc-symbol-heading doc-symbol-class"></code>      <span class="doc doc-object-name doc-class-name">ToolNode</span>") components, or implement your own tool-executing node that collects `Command` objects returned by the tools and returns a list of them, e.g.:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-24-1)defcall_tools(state):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-24-2)  ...
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-24-3)  commands = [tools_by_name[tool_call["name"]].invoke(tool_call) for tool_call in tool_calls]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-24-4)  return commands

```

### Long-term memory[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#long-term-memory "Permanent link")
Use [long-term memory](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/memory/#long-term-memory) to store user-specific or application-specific data across conversations. This is useful for applications like chatbots, where you want to remember user preferences or other information.
To use long-term memory, you need to:
  1. [Configure a store](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/memory/add-memory/#add-long-term-memory) to persist data across invocations.
  2. Use the [`get_store`](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/config/#langgraph.config.get_store "<code class="doc-symbol doc-symbol-heading doc-symbol-function"></code>      <span class="doc doc-object-name doc-function-name">get_store</span>") function to access the store from within tools or prompts.


To **access** information in the store:
_API Reference:[RunnableConfig](https://python.langchain.com/api_reference/core/runnables/langchain_core.runnables.config.RunnableConfig.html?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.116.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296) | [tool](https://python.langchain.com/api_reference/core/tools/langchain_core.tools.convert.tool.html?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.116.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296) | [StateGraph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/graphs/#langgraph.graph.state.StateGraph) | [get_store](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/config/#langgraph.config.get_store)_
```

## Advanced tool features[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#advanced-tool-features "Permanent link")
### Immediate return[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#immediate-return "Permanent link")
Use `return_direct=True` to immediately return a tool's result without executing additional logic.
This is useful for tools that should not trigger further processing or tool calls, allowing you to return results directly to the user.
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-29-1)@tool(return_direct=True)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-29-2)defadd(a: int, b: int) -> int:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-29-3)"""Add two numbers"""
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-29-4)  return a + b

```

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-30-9)agent = create_react_agent(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-30-10)  model="anthropic:claude-3-7-sonnet-latest",
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-30-11)  tools=[add]

Using without prebuilt components
If you are building a custom workflow and are not relying on `create_react_agent` or `ToolNode`, you will also need to implement the control flow to handle `return_direct=True`.
### Force tool use[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#force-tool-use "Permanent link")
If you need to force a specific tool to be used, you will need to configure this at the **model** level using the `tool_choice` parameter in the `bind_tools` method.
Force specific tool usage via tool_choice:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-31-1)@tool(return_direct=True)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-31-2)defgreet(user_name: str) -> int:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-31-3)"""Greet user."""
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-31-4)  return f"Hello {user_name}!"
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-31-5)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-31-6)tools = [greet]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-31-7)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-31-8)configured_model = model.bind_tools(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-31-9)  tools,
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-31-10)  # Force the use of the 'greet' tool
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-31-11)  tool_choice={"type": "tool", "name": "greet"}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-31-12))

```

Extended example: Force tool usage in an agent
To force the agent to use specific tools, you can set the `tool_choice` option in `model.bind_tools()`:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-32-1)fromlangchain_core.toolsimport tool
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-32-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-32-3)@tool(return_direct=True)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-32-4)defgreet(user_name: str) -> int:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-32-5)"""Greet user."""
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-32-6)  return f"Hello {user_name}!"
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-32-7)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-32-8)tools = [greet]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-32-9)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-32-10)agent = create_react_agent(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-32-11)  model=model.bind_tools(tools, tool_choice={"type": "tool", "name": "greet"}),
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-32-12)  tools=tools
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-32-13))
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-32-14)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-32-15)agent.invoke(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-32-16)  {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hi, I am Bob"}]}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-32-17))

```

Avoid infinite loops
Forcing tool usage without stopping conditions can create infinite loops. Use one of the following safeguards:
  * Mark the tool with [`return_direct=True`](#immediate-return to end the loop after execution.
  * Set [`recursion_limit`](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/#recursion-limit) to restrict the number of execution steps.


Tool choice configuration
The `tool_choice` parameter is used to configure which tool should be used by the model when it decides to call a tool. This is useful when you want to ensure that a specific tool is always called for a particular task or when you want to override the model's default behavior of choosing a tool based on its internal logic.
Note that not all models support this feature, and the exact configuration may vary depending on the model you are using.
### Disable parallel calls[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#disable-parallel-calls "Permanent link")
For supported providers, you can disable parallel tool calling by setting `parallel_tool_calls=False` via the `model.bind_tools()` method:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-33-1)model.bind_tools(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-33-2)  tools, 
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-33-3)  parallel_tool_calls=False
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-33-4))

```

Extended example: disable parallel tool calls in a prebuilt agent
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-34-1)fromlangchain.chat_modelsimport init_chat_model
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-34-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-34-3)defadd(a: int, b: int) -> int:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-34-4)"""Add two numbers"""
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-34-5)  return a + b
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-34-6)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-34-7)defmultiply(a: int, b: int) -> int:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-34-8)"""Multiply two numbers."""
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-34-9)  return a * b
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-34-10)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-34-11)model = init_chat_model("anthropic:claude-3-5-sonnet-latest", temperature=0)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-34-12)tools = [add, multiply]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-34-13)agent = create_react_agent(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-34-14)  # disable parallel tool calls
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-34-15)  model=model.bind_tools(tools, parallel_tool_calls=False),
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-34-16)  tools=tools
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-34-17))
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-34-18)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-34-19)agent.invoke(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-34-20)  {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "what's 3 + 5 and 4 * 7?"}]}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-34-21))

```

### Handle errors[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#handle-errors "Permanent link")
LangGraph provides built-in error handling for tool execution through the prebuilt [ToolNode](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/agents/#langgraph.prebuilt.tool_node.ToolNode "<code class="doc-symbol doc-symbol-heading doc-symbol-class"></code>      <span class="doc doc-object-name doc-class-name">ToolNode</span>") component, used both independently and in prebuilt agents.
By **default** , `ToolNode` catches exceptions raised during tool execution and returns them as `ToolMessage` objects with a status indicating an error.
_API Reference:[AIMessage](https://python.langchain.com/api_reference/core/messages/langchain_core.messages.ai.AIMessage.html?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.116.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296) | [ToolNode](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/prebuilt/#langgraph.prebuilt.tool_node.ToolNode)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-1)fromlangchain_core.messagesimport AIMessage
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-2)fromlanggraph.prebuiltimport ToolNode
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-3)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-4)defmultiply(a: int, b: int) -> int:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-5)  if a == 42:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-6)    raise ValueError("The ultimate error")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-7)  return a * b
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-8)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-9)# Default error handling (enabled by default)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-10)tool_node = ToolNode([multiply])
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-11)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-12)message = AIMessage(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-13)  content="",
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-14)  tool_calls=[{
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-15)    "name": "multiply",
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-16)    "args": {"a": 42, "b": 7},
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-17)    "id": "tool_call_id",
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-18)    "type": "tool_call"
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-19)  }]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-20))
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-21)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-35-22)result = tool_node.invoke({"messages": [message]})

```

Output:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-36-1){'messages': [
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-36-2)  ToolMessage(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-36-3)    content="Error: ValueError('The ultimate error')\n Please fix your mistakes.",
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-36-4)    name='multiply',
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-36-5)    tool_call_id='tool_call_id',
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-36-6)    status='error'
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-36-7)  )
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-36-8)]}

```

#### Disable error handling[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#disable-error-handling "Permanent link")
To propagate exceptions directly, disable error handling:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-37-1)tool_node = ToolNode([multiply], handle_tool_errors=False)

```

With error handling disabled, exceptions raised by tools will propagate up, requiring explicit management.
#### Custom error messages[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#custom-error-messages "Permanent link")
Provide a custom error message by setting `handle_tool_errors` to a string:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-38-1)tool_node = ToolNode(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-38-2)  [multiply],
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-38-3)  handle_tool_errors="Can't use 42 as the first operand, please switch operands!"
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-38-4))

```

Example output:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-39-1){'messages': [
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-39-2)  ToolMessage(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-39-3)    content="Can't use 42 as the first operand, please switch operands!",
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-39-4)    name='multiply',
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-39-5)    tool_call_id='tool_call_id',
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-39-6)    status='error'
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-39-7)  )
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-39-8)]}

```

#### Error handling in agents[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#error-handling-in-agents "Permanent link")
Error handling in prebuilt agents (`create_react_agent`) leverages `ToolNode`:
_API Reference:[create_react_agent](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/prebuilt/#langgraph.prebuilt.chat_agent_executor.create_react_agent)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-40-1)fromlanggraph.prebuiltimport create_react_agent
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-40-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-40-3)agent = create_react_agent(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-40-4)  model="anthropic:claude-3-7-sonnet-latest",
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-40-5)  tools=[multiply]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-40-6))
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-40-7)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-40-8)# Default error handling
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-40-9)agent.invoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "what's 42 x 7?"}]})

```

To disable or customize error handling in prebuilt agents, explicitly pass a configured `ToolNode`:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-41-1)custom_tool_node = ToolNode(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-41-2)  [multiply],
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-41-3)  handle_tool_errors="Cannot use 42 as a first operand!"
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-41-4))
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-41-5)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-41-6)agent_custom = create_react_agent(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-41-7)  model="anthropic:claude-3-7-sonnet-latest",
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-41-8)  tools=custom_tool_node
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-41-9))
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-41-10)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-41-11)agent_custom.invoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "what's 42 x 7?"}]})

```

### Handle large numbers of tools[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#handle-large-numbers-of-tools "Permanent link")
As the number of available tools grows, you may want to limit the scope of the LLM's selection, to decrease token consumption and to help manage sources of error in LLM reasoning.
To address this, you can dynamically adjust the tools available to a model by retrieving relevant tools at runtime using semantic search.
See [`langgraph-bigtool`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph-bigtool) prebuilt library for a ready-to-use implementation.
## Prebuilt tools[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#prebuilt-tools "Permanent link")
### LLM provider tools[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#llm-provider-tools "Permanent link")
You can use prebuilt tools from model providers by passing a dictionary with tool specs to the `tools` parameter of `create_react_agent`. For example, to use the `web_search_preview` tool from OpenAI:
_API Reference:[create_react_agent](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/prebuilt/#langgraph.prebuilt.chat_agent_executor.create_react_agent)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-42-1)fromlanggraph.prebuiltimport create_react_agent
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-42-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-42-3)agent = create_react_agent(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-42-4)  model="openai:gpt-4o-mini", 
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-42-5)  tools=[{"type": "web_search_preview"}]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-42-6))
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-42-7)response = agent.invoke(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-42-8)  {"messages": ["What was a positive news story from today?"]}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#__codelineno-42-9))

```

Please consult the documentation for the specific model you are using to see which tools are available and how to use them.
### LangChain tools[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/tool-calling/#langchain-tools "Permanent link")
Additionally, LangChain supports a wide range of prebuilt tool integrations for interacting with APIs, databases, file systems, web data, and more. These tools extend the functionality of agents and enable rapid development.
You can browse the full list of available integrations in the [LangChain integrations directory](https://python.langchain.com/docs/integrations/tools/?__hstc=5909356.7a78626991ea6b97c086bc6628d532dd.1752857917661.1752857917661.1752857917661.1&__hssc=5909356.116.1752857917662&__hsfp=2807806296).
Some commonly used tool categories include:
  * **Search** : Bing, SerpAPI, Tavily
  * **Code interpreters** : Python REPL, Node.js REPL
  * **Databases** : SQL, MongoDB, Redis
  * **Web data** : Web scraping and browsing
  * **APIs** : OpenWeatherMap, NewsAPI, and others


These integrations can be configured and added to your agents using the same `tools` parameter shown in the examples above.

# Use the functional API[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#use-the-functional-api "Permanent link")
The [**Functional API**](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/functional_api/) allows you to add LangGraph's key features — [persistence](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/persistence/), [memory](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/memory/add-memory/), [human-in-the-loop](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/human_in_the_loop/), and [streaming](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/streaming/) — to your applications with minimal changes to your existing code.
Tip
For conceptual information on the functional API, see [Functional API](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/functional_api/).
## Creating a simple workflow[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#creating-a-simple-workflow "Permanent link")
When defining an `entrypoint`, input is restricted to the first argument of the function. To pass multiple inputs, you can use a dictionary.
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-0-1)@entrypoint(checkpointer=checkpointer)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-0-2)defmy_workflow(inputs: dict) -> int:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-0-3)  value = inputs["value"]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-0-4)  another_value = inputs["another_value"]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-0-5)  ...
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-0-6)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-0-7)my_workflow.invoke({"value": 1, "another_value": 2}) 

```

Extended example: simple workflow
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-1)importuuid
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-2)fromlanggraph.funcimport entrypoint, task
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-3)fromlanggraph.checkpoint.memoryimport MemorySaver
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-4)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-5)# Task that checks if a number is even
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-6)@task
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-7)defis_even(number: int) -> bool:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-8)  return number % 2 == 0
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-9)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-10)# Task that formats a message
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-11)@task
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-12)defformat_message(is_even: bool) -> str:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-13)  return "The number is even." if is_even else "The number is odd."
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-14)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-15)# Create a checkpointer for persistence
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-16)checkpointer = MemorySaver()
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-17)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-18)@entrypoint(checkpointer=checkpointer)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-19)defworkflow(inputs: dict) -> str:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-20)"""Simple workflow to classify a number."""
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-21)  even = is_even(inputs["number"]).result()
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-22)  return format_message(even).result()
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-23)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-24)# Run the workflow with a unique thread ID
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-25)config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": str(uuid.uuid4())}}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-26)result = workflow.invoke({"number": 7}, config=config)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-1-27)print(result)

```

Extended example: Compose an essay with an LLM
This example demonstrates how to use the `@task` and `@entrypoint` decorators syntactically. Given that a checkpointer is provided, the workflow results will be persisted in the checkpointer.
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-1)importuuid
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-2)fromlangchain.chat_modelsimport init_chat_model
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-3)fromlanggraph.funcimport entrypoint, task
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-4)fromlanggraph.checkpoint.memoryimport MemorySaver
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-5)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-6)llm = init_chat_model('openai:gpt-3.5-turbo')
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-7)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-8)# Task: generate essay using an LLM
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-9)@task
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-10)defcompose_essay(topic: str) -> str:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-11)"""Generate an essay about the given topic."""
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-12)  return llm.invoke([
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-13)    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant that writes essays."},
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-14)    {"role": "user", "content": f"Write an essay about {topic}."}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-15)  ]).content
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-16)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-17)# Create a checkpointer for persistence
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-18)checkpointer = MemorySaver()
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-19)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-20)@entrypoint(checkpointer=checkpointer)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-21)defworkflow(topic: str) -> str:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-22)"""Simple workflow that generates an essay with an LLM."""
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-23)  return compose_essay(topic).result()
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-24)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-25)# Execute the workflow
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-26)config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": str(uuid.uuid4())}}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-27)result = workflow.invoke("the history of flight", config=config)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-2-28)print(result)

```

## Parallel execution[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#parallel-execution "Permanent link")
Tasks can be executed in parallel by invoking them concurrently and waiting for the results. This is useful for improving performance in IO bound tasks (e.g., calling APIs for LLMs).
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-3-1)@task
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-3-2)defadd_one(number: int) -> int:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-3-3)  return number + 1
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-3-4)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-3-5)@entrypoint(checkpointer=checkpointer)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-3-6)defgraph(numbers: list[int]) -> list[str]:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-3-7)  futures = [add_one(i) for i in numbers]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-3-8)  return [f.result() for f in futures]

```

Extended example: parallel LLM calls
This example demonstrates how to run multiple LLM calls in parallel using `@task`. Each call generates a paragraph on a different topic, and results are joined into a single text output.
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-1)importuuid
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-2)fromlangchain.chat_modelsimport init_chat_model
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-3)fromlanggraph.funcimport entrypoint, task
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-4)fromlanggraph.checkpoint.memoryimport MemorySaver
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-5)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-6)# Initialize the LLM model
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-7)llm = init_chat_model("openai:gpt-3.5-turbo")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-8)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-9)# Task that generates a paragraph about a given topic
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-10)@task
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-11)defgenerate_paragraph(topic: str) -> str:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-12)  response = llm.invoke([
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-13)    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant that writes educational paragraphs."},
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-14)    {"role": "user", "content": f"Write a paragraph about {topic}."}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-15)  ])
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-16)  return response.content
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-17)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-18)# Create a checkpointer for persistence
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-19)checkpointer = MemorySaver()
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-20)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-21)@entrypoint(checkpointer=checkpointer)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-22)defworkflow(topics: list[str]) -> str:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-23)"""Generates multiple paragraphs in parallel and combines them."""
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-24)  futures = [generate_paragraph(topic) for topic in topics]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-25)  paragraphs = [f.result() for f in futures]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-26)  return "\n\n".join(paragraphs)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-27)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-28)# Run the workflow
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-29)config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": str(uuid.uuid4())}}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-30)result = workflow.invoke(["quantum computing", "climate change", "history of aviation"], config=config)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-4-31)print(result)

```

This example uses LangGraph's concurrency model to improve execution time, especially when tasks involve I/O like LLM completions.
## Calling graphs[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#calling-graphs "Permanent link")
The **Functional API** and the [**Graph API**](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/low_level/) can be used together in the same application as they share the same underlying runtime.
_API Reference:[entrypoint](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/func/#langgraph.func.entrypoint) | [StateGraph](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/graphs/#langgraph.graph.state.StateGraph)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-5-1)fromlanggraph.funcimport entrypoint

## Call other entrypoints[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#call-other-entrypoints "Permanent link")
You can call other **entrypoints** from within an **entrypoint** or a **task**.
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-7-1)@entrypoint() # Will automatically use the checkpointer from the parent entrypoint
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-7-2)defsome_other_workflow(inputs: dict) -> int:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-7-3)  return inputs["value"]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-7-4)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-7-5)@entrypoint(checkpointer=checkpointer)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-7-6)defmy_workflow(inputs: dict) -> int:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-7-7)  value = some_other_workflow.invoke({"value": 1})
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-7-8)  return value

```

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-8-7)

## Streaming[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#streaming "Permanent link")
The **Functional API** uses the same streaming mechanism as the **Graph API**. Please read the [**streaming guide**](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/streaming/) section for more details.

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-14-12)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-14-13)@entrypoint(cache=InMemoryCache())
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-14-14)defmain(inputs: dict) -> dict[str, int]:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-14-15)  result1 = slow_add(inputs["x"]).result()
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-14-16)  result2 = slow_add(inputs["x"]).result()
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-14-17)  return {"result1": result1, "result2": result2}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-14-18)

## Resuming after an error[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#resuming-after-an-error "Permanent link")
_API Reference:[MemorySaver](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/checkpoints/#langgraph.checkpoint.memory.MemorySaver) | [entrypoint](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/func/#langgraph.func.entrypoint) | [task](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/func/#langgraph.func.task) | [StreamWriter](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/types/#langgraph.types.StreamWriter)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-1)importtime
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-2)fromlanggraph.checkpoint.memoryimport MemorySaver
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-3)fromlanggraph.funcimport entrypoint, task
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-4)fromlanggraph.typesimport StreamWriter
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-5)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-6)# This variable is just used for demonstration purposes to simulate a network failure.
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-7)# It's not something you will have in your actual code.
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-8)attempts = 0
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-9)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-10)@task()
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-11)defget_info():
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-12)"""
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-13)  Simulates a task that fails once before succeeding.
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-14)  Raises an exception on the first attempt, then returns "OK" on subsequent tries.
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-15)  """
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-16)  global attempts
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-17)  attempts += 1
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-18)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-19)  if attempts < 2:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-20)    raise ValueError("Failure") # Simulate a failure on the first attempt
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-21)  return "OK"
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-22)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-23)# Initialize an in-memory checkpointer for persistence
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-24)checkpointer = MemorySaver()
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-25)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-26)@task
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-27)defslow_task():
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-28)"""
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-29)  Simulates a slow-running task by introducing a 1-second delay.
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-30)  """
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-31)  time.sleep(1)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-32)  return "Ran slow task."
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-33)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-34)@entrypoint(checkpointer=checkpointer)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-35)defmain(inputs, writer: StreamWriter):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-36)"""
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-37)  Main workflow function that runs the slow_task and get_info tasks sequentially.
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-38)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-39)  Parameters:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-40)  - inputs: Dictionary containing workflow input values.
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-41)  - writer: StreamWriter for streaming custom data.
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-42)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-43)  The workflow first executes `slow_task` and then attempts to execute `get_info`,
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-44)  which will fail on the first invocation.
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-45)  """
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-46)  slow_task_result = slow_task().result() # Blocking call to slow_task
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-47)  get_info().result() # Exception will be raised here on the first attempt
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-48)  return slow_task_result
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-49)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-50)# Workflow execution configuration with a unique thread identifier
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-51)config = {
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-52)  "configurable": {
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-53)    "thread_id": "1" # Unique identifier to track workflow execution
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-54)  }
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-55)}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-56)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-57)# This invocation will take ~1 second due to the slow_task execution
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-58)try:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-59)  # First invocation will raise an exception due to the `get_info` task failing
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-60)  main.invoke({'any_input': 'foobar'}, config=config)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-61)except ValueError:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-15-62)  pass # Handle the failure gracefully

```

When we resume execution, we won't need to re-run the `slow_task` as its result is already saved in the checkpoint.
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-16-1)main.invoke(None, config=config)

```

```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-17-1)'Ran slow task.'

```

## Human-in-the-loop[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#human-in-the-loop "Permanent link")
The functional API supports [human-in-the-loop](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/human_in_the_loop/) workflows using the `interrupt` function and the `Command` primitive.
### Basic human-in-the-loop workflow[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#basic-human-in-the-loop-workflow "Permanent link")
We will create three [tasks](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/functional_api/#task):
  1. Append `"bar"`.
  2. Pause for human input. When resuming, append human input.
  3. Append `"qux"`.


_API Reference:[entrypoint](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/func/#langgraph.func.entrypoint) | [task](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/func/#langgraph.func.task) | [Command](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/types/#langgraph.types.Command) | [interrupt](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/types/#langgraph.types.interrupt)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-18-1)fromlanggraph.funcimport entrypoint, task
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-18-2)fromlanggraph.typesimport Command, interrupt
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-18-3)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-18-4)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-18-5)@task
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-18-6)defstep_1(input_query):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-18-7)"""Append bar."""
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-18-8)  return f"{input_query} bar"
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-18-9)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-18-10)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-18-11)@task
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-18-12)defhuman_feedback(input_query):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-18-13)"""Append user input."""
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-18-14)  feedback = interrupt(f"Please provide feedback: {input_query}")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-18-15)  return f"{input_query}{feedback}"
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-18-16)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-18-17)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-18-18)@task
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-18-19)defstep_3(input_query):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-18-20)"""Append qux."""
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-18-21)  return f"{input_query} qux"

```

We can now compose these tasks in an [entrypoint](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/functional_api/#entrypoint):
_API Reference:[MemorySaver](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/checkpoints/#langgraph.checkpoint.memory.MemorySaver)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-19-1)fromlanggraph.checkpoint.memoryimport MemorySaver
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-19-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-19-3)checkpointer = MemorySaver()
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-19-4)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-19-5)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-19-6)@entrypoint(checkpointer=checkpointer)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-19-7)defgraph(input_query):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-19-8)  result_1 = step_1(input_query).result()
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-19-9)  result_2 = human_feedback(result_1).result()
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-19-10)  result_3 = step_3(result_2).result()
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-19-11)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-19-12)  return result_3

```

[interrupt()](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/human_in_the_loop/add-human-in-the-loop/#pause-using-interrupt) is called inside a task, enabling a human to review and edit the output of the previous task. The results of prior tasks-- in this case `step_1`-- are persisted, so that they are not run again following the `interrupt`.
Let's send in a query string:
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-20-1)config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-20-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-20-3)for event in graph.stream("foo", config):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-20-4)  print(event)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-20-5)  print("\n")

```

Note that we've paused with an `interrupt` after `step_1`. The interrupt provides instructions to resume the run. To resume, we issue a [Command](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/human_in_the_loop/add-human-in-the-loop/#resume-using-the-command-primitive) containing the data expected by the `human_feedback` task.
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-21-1)# Continue execution
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-21-2)for event in graph.stream(Command(resume="baz"), config):
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-21-3)  print(event)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-21-4)  print("\n")

```

After resuming, the run proceeds through the remaining step and terminates as expected. 
### Review tool calls[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#review-tool-calls "Permanent link")
To review tool calls before execution, we add a `review_tool_call` function that calls [`interrupt`](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/human_in_the_loop/add-human-in-the-loop/#pause-using-interrupt). When this function is called, execution will be paused until we issue a command to resume it.
Given a tool call, our function will `interrupt` for human review. At that point we can either:
  * Accept the tool call
  * Revise the tool call and continue
  * Generate a custom tool message (e.g., instructing the model to re-format its tool call)


```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-22-1)fromtypingimport Union
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-22-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-22-3)defreview_tool_call(tool_call: ToolCall) -> Union[ToolCall, ToolMessage]:
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-22-4)"""Review a tool call, returning a validated version."""
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-22-5)  human_review = interrupt(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-22-6)    {
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-22-7)      "question": "Is this correct?",
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-22-8)      "tool_call": tool_call,
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-22-9)    }
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-22-10)  )
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-22-11)  review_action = human_review["action"]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-22-12)  review_data = human_review.get("data")
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-22-13)  if review_action == "continue":
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-22-14)    return tool_call
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-22-15)  elif review_action == "update":
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-22-16)    updated_tool_call = {**tool_call, **{"args": review_data}}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-22-17)    return updated_tool_call
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-22-18)  elif review_action == "feedback":
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-22-19)    return ToolMessage(
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-22-20)      content=review_data, name=tool_call["name"], tool_call_id=tool_call["id"]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-22-21)    )

```

We can now update our [entrypoint](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/functional_api/#entrypoint) to review the generated tool calls. If a tool call is accepted or revised, we execute in the same way as before. Otherwise, we just append the `ToolMessage` supplied by the human. The results of prior tasks — in this case the initial model call — are persisted, so that they are not run again following the `interrupt`.
_API Reference:[MemorySaver](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/checkpoints/#langgraph.checkpoint.memory.MemorySaver) | [add_messages](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/graphs/#langgraph.graph.message.add_messages) | [Command](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/types/#langgraph.types.Command) | [interrupt](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/types/#langgraph.types.interrupt)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-23-1)fromlanggraph.checkpoint.memoryimport MemorySaver

## Short-term memory[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#short-term-memory "Permanent link")
Short-term memory allows storing information across different **invocations** of the same **thread id**. See [short-term memory](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/functional_api/#short-term-memory) for more details.
### Manage checkpoints[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#manage-checkpoints "Permanent link")
You can view and delete the information stored by the checkpointer.

### Decouple return value from saved value[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#decouple-return-value-from-saved-value "Permanent link")
Use `entrypoint.final` to decouple what is returned to the caller from what is persisted in the checkpoint. This is useful when:
  * You want to return a computed result (e.g., a summary or status), but save a different internal value for use on the next invocation.
  * You need to control what gets passed to the previous parameter on the next run.


_API Reference:[entrypoint](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/func/#langgraph.func.entrypoint) | [MemorySaver](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/reference/checkpoints/#langgraph.checkpoint.memory.MemorySaver)_
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#__codelineno-28-1)fromtypingimport Optional

## Long-term memory[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-functional-api/#long-term-memory "Permanent link")
[long-term memory](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/memory/#long-term-memory) allows storing information across different **thread ids**. This could be useful for learning information about a given user in one conversation and using it in another.

# How to interact with the deployment using RemoteGraph[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#how-to-interact-with-the-deployment-using-remotegraph "Permanent link")
Prerequisites
  * [LangGraph Platform](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/langgraph_platform/)
  * [LangGraph Server](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/concepts/langgraph_server/)


`RemoteGraph` is an interface that allows you to interact with your LangGraph Platform deployment as if it were a regular, locally-defined LangGraph graph (e.g. a `CompiledGraph`). This guide shows you how you can initialize a `RemoteGraph` and interact with it.
## Initializing the graph[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#initializing-the-graph "Permanent link")
When initializing a `RemoteGraph`, you must always specify:
  * `name`: the name of the graph you want to interact with. This is the same graph name you use in `langgraph.json` configuration file for your deployment. 
  * `api_key`: a valid LangSmith API key. Can be set as an environment variable (`LANGSMITH_API_KEY`) or passed directly via the `api_key` argument. The API key could also be provided via the `client` / `sync_client` arguments, if `LangGraphClient` / `SyncLangGraphClient` were initialized with `api_key` argument.


Additionally, you have to provide one of the following:
  * `url`: URL of the deployment you want to interact with. If you pass `url` argument, both sync and async clients will be created using the provided URL, headers (if provided) and default configuration values (e.g. timeout, etc).
  * `client`: a `LangGraphClient` instance for interacting with the deployment asynchronously (e.g. using `.astream()`, `.ainvoke()`, `.aget_state()`, `.aupdate_state()`, etc.)
  * `sync_client`: a `SyncLangGraphClient` instance for interacting with the deployment synchronously (e.g. using `.stream()`, `.invoke()`, `.get_state()`, `.update_state()`, etc.)


Note
If you pass both `client` or `sync_client` as well as `url` argument, they will take precedence over the `url` argument. If none of the `client` / `sync_client` / `url` arguments are provided, `RemoteGraph` will raise a `ValueError` at runtime.
### Using URL[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#using-url "Permanent link")
[Python](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__tabbed_1_1)[JavaScript](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__tabbed_1_2)
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-0-1)fromlanggraph.pregel.remoteimport RemoteGraph
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-0-2)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-0-3)url = <DEPLOYMENT_URL>
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-0-4)graph_name = "agent"
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-0-5)remote_graph = RemoteGraph(graph_name, url=url)

```

```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-1-1)import{RemoteGraph}from"@langchain/langgraph/remote";
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-1-2)

### Using clients[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#using-clients "Permanent link")
[Python](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__tabbed_2_1)[JavaScript](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__tabbed_2_2)
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-2-1)fromlanggraph_sdkimport get_client, get_sync_client
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-2-2)fromlanggraph.pregel.remoteimport RemoteGraph
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-2-3)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-2-4)url = <DEPLOYMENT_URL>
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-2-5)graph_name = "agent"
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-2-6)client = get_client(url=url)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-2-7)sync_client = get_sync_client(url=url)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-2-8)remote_graph = RemoteGraph(graph_name, client=client, sync_client=sync_client)

```

## Invoking the graph[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#invoking-the-graph "Permanent link")
Since `RemoteGraph` is a `Runnable` that implements the same methods as `CompiledGraph`, you can interact with it the same way you normally would with a compiled graph, i.e. by calling `.invoke()`, `.stream()`, `.get_state()`, `.update_state()`, etc (as well as their async counterparts).
### Asynchronously[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#asynchronously "Permanent link")
Note
To use the graph asynchronously, you must provide either the `url` or `client` when initializing the `RemoteGraph`.
[Python](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__tabbed_3_1)[JavaScript](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__tabbed_3_2)
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-4-1)# invoke the graph
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-4-2)result = await remote_graph.ainvoke({
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-4-3)  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "what's the weather in sf"}]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-4-4)})

### Synchronously[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#synchronously "Permanent link")

## Thread-level persistence[¶](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#thread-level-persistence "Permanent link")
By default, the graph runs (i.e. `.invoke()` or `.stream()` invocations) are stateless - the checkpoints and the final state of the graph are not persisted. If you would like to persist the outputs of the graph run (for example, to enable human-in-the-loop features), you can create a thread and provide the thread ID via the `config` argument, same as you would with a regular compiled graph:
[Python](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__tabbed_5_1)[JavaScript](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__tabbed_5_2)
```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-7-1)fromlanggraph_sdkimport get_sync_client
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-7-2)url = <DEPLOYMENT_URL>
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-7-3)graph_name = "agent"
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-7-4)sync_client = get_sync_client(url=url)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-7-5)remote_graph = RemoteGraph(graph_name, url=url)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-7-6)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-7-7)# create a thread (or use an existing thread instead)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-7-8)thread = sync_client.threads.create()
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-7-9)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-7-10)# invoke the graph with the thread config
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-7-11)config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": thread["thread_id"]}}
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-7-12)result = remote_graph.invoke({
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-7-13)  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "what's the weather in sf"}]
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-7-14)}, config=config)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-7-15)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-7-16)# verify that the state was persisted to the thread
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-7-17)thread_state = remote_graph.get_state(config)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-7-18)print(thread_state)

```

```
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-8-1)import{Client}from"@langchain/langgraph-sdk";
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-8-2)import{RemoteGraph}from"@langchain/langgraph/remote";
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-8-3)

[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-8-11)
[](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/how-tos/use-remote-graph/#__codelineno-8-12)// invoke the graph with the thread config
